extracted.intended_audience: media critics, journalists, media-watchers, and the general public interested in press accountability
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and norms for responsible reporting and for when news organizations should correct or retract stories, illustrated by the CNN 'Tailwind' episode and historical examples of uncorrected reporting. Focus is on editorial practices, sourcing, independence, and institutional accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreaching claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting should not 'overreach' beyond what the evidence supports; the Tailwind reports were described as 'marred by overreaching' when they asserted sarin nerve gas use without adequate corroboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not draw definitive conclusions when evidence is disputed or incomplete. Flag uncertainty, avoid sensational assertions, and ensure headlines and on-air language reflect the strength of the evidence. Anti-pattern: presenting a contested allegation as settled fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include and preserve dissenting testimony and expert dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Give adequate airtime and prominence to witnesses and experts who dispute the primary conclusion — the piece notes 'inadequate time given to Tailwind veterans and experts who disputed the conclusion that sarin had been used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that contradictory on-the-record comments are not edited out of the final presentation. Example: a pilot's comment that tear gas, not nerve gas, had been deployed was reportedly deleted in final edits; such deletions undermine balance and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient time and context for complex stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex investigations require adequate runtime and contextual depth — producers argued their report 'needed a full hour' but was cut to an 18-minute segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When subject matter is complicated (historical military operations, chemical-weapons claims), allocate enough time/space to present nuance, background, and counter-arguments. Condensed formats risk oversimplification and misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify extraordinary claims with robust sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of chemical-weapons use (e.g., sarin) require rigorous verification; anecdotal on-the-record comments alone are insufficient for extraordinary allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate with independent expert analysis, scientific testing, multiple credible eyewitnesses, and documentary evidence before asserting use of chemical agents. Anti-pattern: relying primarily on a few on-camera testimonies for high-stakes allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain editorial independence from PR and power-center pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations must resist treating controversies as 'PR problems' and avoid letting external pressure (military, political, or institutional) dictate coverage decisions — CNN management reportedly framed criticism as a 'PR problem.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should insulate news judgment from institutional reputation-management concerns and from pressure by officials or powerful figures. Watch for patterns where criticism from power centers leads to retraction without transparent journalistic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be willing to correct and retract transparently and consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting fails editorial standards, organizations should 'set the record straight' via corrections or retractions; the piece criticizes selective retractions and notes many prominent stories (e.g., Gulf of Tonkin, 'yellow rain') went un-retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply correction/retraction standards consistently regardless of whether the story supports or challenges government positions. Provide clear explanations of errors and how they occurred. Anti-pattern: selective retraction only when political pressure is overwhelming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and support investigative journalists from managerial muzzling or retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers were reportedly 'muzzled by management' after the Tailwind broadcast and later fired; the article implies organizations should not punish reporters for pursuing difficult investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should defend journalists who follow editorial standards and allow them to pursue follow-up reporting. Retaliation or silencing of reporters is an indicator of organizational failure to uphold journalistic norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accountability in the editorial chain of command
rubrics_metrics.description: Final editorial responsibility must be clear and exercised with journalistic, not purely corporate or PR, priorities — the article notes that 'top CNN executives in the final edit deleted a comment' and then later hired attorneys to investigate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document editorial decisions, preserve original materials and assembly edits, and make accountable who made substantive changes. Transparency about the final-edit process helps evaluate responsibility for errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer independent, transparent investigations over opaque internal handling
rubrics_metrics.description: CNN's response involved hiring outside attorney Floyd Abrams alongside internal counsel; the piece raises questions about whether investigations are sufficiently independent and transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing whether a network has properly investigated errors, look for genuinely independent review, publication of findings or summaries, and clear remediation steps. Anti-pattern: opaque internal probes that prioritize legal/PR containment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using celebrity correspondents as marketing at the expense of accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The article reports that Peter Arnett was used 'mainly for star power and “marketing purposes”' and was spared responsibility, suggesting a problem when personalities shield networks from accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow presence of high-profile names to substitute for rigorous reporting standards or to deflect responsibility. Assign clear authorship and responsibility regardless of correspondent celebrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold outlets to historical accountability — revisit and correct major past errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Major historical reporting errors (Gulf of Tonkin, 'yellow rain', false Soviet/Bulgarian attribution for the Pope shooting) often went uncorrected; the piece argues for retractions or at least acknowledgment even of older high-impact mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should be willing to examine and correct past coverage when new evidence shows serious error, not only recent or politically convenient cases. Large-scale or systemic falsehoods merit public retraction or retrospective coverage.
